nodes.title: 命题（proposition）
misconceptions: 把疑问句或祈使句当成命题（What time is it? / Read this carefully. 只是提问或命令，没有真值）
把含未赋值变量的句子当成命题（x + 1 = 2 既不为真也不为假，只有给变量赋值之后才成为命题）
因为自己不知道真假就断定某句不是命题（命题只要求客观上非真即假，不要求我们知道答案）

nodes.title: 复合命题与逻辑联结词（compound proposition / logical connectives）
misconceptions: 把 ¬p ∧ q 读成 ¬(p ∧ q)（否定运算符先于所有二元运算符作用）
以为合取与析取之间没有优先级，把 p ∨ q ∧ r 读成 (p ∨ q) ∧ r
以为条件运算符优先于析取，把 p → q ∨ r 读成 (p → q) ∨ r

nodes.title: 真值表（truth table）
misconceptions: 命题变元只写一行真值，漏掉另一种可能（每个变元都要取遍真与假）
把中间子表达式的列当成最终结果，不知道最后一列才是整个复合命题的真值

nodes.title: 否定（negation）
misconceptions: 把 has at least 32 GB of memory 的否定写成 has at most 32 GB（正确否定是 has less than 32 GB）
把否定理解成换一句意思相反的话，而不是把原命题的真值取反

nodes.title: 合取（conjunction）
misconceptions: 认为 but 不能算合取（The sun is shining, but it is raining 就是两个命题的合取）
把合取的真值条件记反，以为有一个为真就为真

nodes.title: 析取（disjunction）
misconceptions: 把析取当成二者只能取其一（析取是相容或，两个都真时仍为真）
看到 or 就直接译成析取，不判断句子本意是相容或还是排斥或

nodes.title: 异或（exclusive or）
misconceptions: 把异或当成至少一个为真（异或要求恰好一个为真，两个都真时为假）
把自然语言里的 or 一律当成异或（学过微积分或计算机导论是相容或）

nodes.title: 条件语句（conditional statement / implication）
misconceptions: 把 p only if q 当成 q → p（only 决定方向：p only if q 与 if p, then q 同义）
前件为假时以为条件语句为假（前件为假时条件语句为真）
把 q is necessary for p 与 p is sufficient for q 的方向搞反（两种说法都等价于 if p, then q）
要求前件与后件之间有因果或语义关联，因而否认 If Juan has a smartphone, then 2 + 3 = 5 是真命题
把编程语言里的 if p then S 当成逻辑蕴含（S 是程序段而不是命题）

nodes.title: 逆命题、否命题与逆否命题（converse, contrapositive, inverse）
misconceptions: 认为逆命题或否命题与原条件语句等价（本节指出这是最常见的逻辑错误之一，只有逆否命题总与原命题同真值）
把逆否命题写成对前件和后件直接取否（逆否命题要先交换前件与后件、再分别取否）
当前件真而后件假时，以为逆命题和否命题也是假的（此时它们都是真的）
把中文的否命题与命题的否定混为一谈

nodes.title: 双条件语句（biconditional）
misconceptions: 把自然语言里的 if..., then... 直接当成双条件（If you finish your meal, then you can have dessert 字面上只断言一个方向，另一个方向只是隐含）
把双条件当成条件语句之外的第三种东西，不知道它与两个方向的条件语句的合取真值完全相同
在两个命题都假时把双条件判为假（同真或同假时双条件都为真）

nodes.title: 位与位串（bit, Boolean variable, bit string）
misconceptions: 把位串的长度当成它表示的数值（长度是位串中位的个数）
把按位运算当成整数的算术运算
记反位与真值的对应（1 表示真、0 表示假）

nodes.title: 逻辑电路（logic circuit / digital circuit）
misconceptions: 以为一个逻辑电路可以同时给出多个输出信号（本节只讨论单输出的逻辑电路，多输出是一般数字电路的情形）
把逻辑电路的输入输出当成抽象命题真假值，忘了它们实际是比特 0（断开）或 1（接通）

nodes.title: 逻辑门（gate）：反相器/非门、或门、与门
misconceptions: 把或门理解成“两个输入只能有一个成立”（两个输入都为 1 时或门输出仍然是 1）
把与门和或门的输出对调（与门输出两个输入的合取，或门输出两个输入的析取）
以为反相器要用与门或或门搭出来，而它本身就是三种基本门之一

nodes.title: 布尔检索（Boolean search）
misconceptions: 把 OR 当成“必须同时包含两个检索词”（OR 匹配含其中一个或两个的记录，要求同时包含的是 AND）
忽略 AND 的优先级高于 OR，把 (NEW AND MEXICO OR ARIZONA) 误读成 NEW AND (MEXICO OR ARIZONA)
以为检索词写得越多结果就越精确（教材指出结果里仍会混入无关页面，例如关于墨西哥的新大学的页面，需要再用 NOT 排除）

nodes.title: 系统规格及其一致性（system specification, consistent）
misconceptions: 只要每条规格单独看都能成立，就断定整套规格一致（一致性要求存在一个赋值让所有规格同时为真）
认为往一致的规格集合里再加一条规格不会破坏一致性（加入“诊断消息没有被重传”后四条规格就变得不一致）

nodes.title: 逻辑谜题（logic puzzle）
misconceptions: 靠直觉逐句试猜答案，不为每个原子断言引入命题变元，也不检验哪种赋值能让全部陈述同时成立
漏掉谜题里的数量条件（例如“只有一句是真的”），只逐句判断真假

nodes.title: 骑士与无赖（knights and knaves）
misconceptions: 把无赖的话当成“有时假有时真”（无赖说的每个陈述都为假，骑士说的每个陈述都为真）
看到“某人说了某句话”就直接把这句话当成真的，忘了先判断说话者是骑士还是无赖

nodes.title: 永真式、矛盾式与偶然式
misconceptions: 把「可满足」当成「永真式」：只要找到一组赋值使命题为真，就说它是永真式
把偶然式（有的赋值真、有的赋值假）说成永真式或矛盾式
把永真式排除在可满足之外（永真式也满足「存在一组赋值使命题为真」）
记反否定关系：矛盾式的否定是永真式，永真式的否定是矛盾式

nodes.title: 逻辑等价（logically equivalent）
misconceptions: 把两式逻辑等价当成一个复合命题，拿它去和别的式子做真值运算（它其实是「对应的双条件式是永真式」这一断言）
把表示逻辑等价的符号当成 ∧、∨ 那样的逻辑联结词
把逻辑等价理解成两个式子写法相同或可以互相「代入字母」
把原文里表示逻辑等价的符号 ⇔ 与双条件联结词 ↔ 当成同一个符号

nodes.title: 条件-析取等价（conditional-disjunction equivalence）
misconceptions: 把条件式改写成析取式时把否定加到后件上（写成「后件的否定或前件」）
把前件与后件一起否定，得到「非前件或非后件」
把条件-析取等价与它的逆否形式当成同一个式子
以为改写后仍含有条件联结词

nodes.title: 条件语句的等价式（Table 7）
misconceptions: 把逆命题（交换前件后件）或否命题（前件后件都取否定）当成与原条件式等价，只有逆否命题才等价
把「条件式的否定」展开成「非前件蕴含非后件」或「前件蕴含非后件」（正确结果是「前件真而后件假」）
把两个条件式的合取与「后件的合取作为结论」这一条写反，前件后件位置对调
对条件式直接套用结合律、分配律或德摩根律来「拆括号」

nodes.title: 双条件语句的等价式（Table 8）
misconceptions: 把双条件式的否定写成「两个变元否定的双条件式」（Table 8 里等价的是原双条件式与「双否定后的双条件式」，否定式对应的是「其中一个变元取否定」的形式）
把双条件式展开成两个条件式的析取，而不是合取
把双条件联结词与表示逻辑等价的符号当成同一个符号

nodes.title: 德摩根律（De Morgan's laws）
misconceptions: 取否定后忘记把联结词换成相反的：把「合取的否定」写成「各成分否定的合取」
只否定其中一个成分，例如把「析取的否定」写成「一个成分否定后仍用析取联结」
把两条律的方向用反：否定合取应该得到各成分否定的析取
把德摩根律用在条件式或双条件式上，当作可以直接「把否定推进去」

nodes.title: 基本逻辑等价律（Table 6）
misconceptions: 把结合律、分配律或德摩根律用在合取与析取混合出现的表达式上（这些律只在所有运算符都相同时才适用）
把两个分配律的方向写错：析取分配到合取、合取分配到析取得到的展开式不同
把同一律与支配律记混（与恒真常元合取保持原式，与恒真常元析取得到恒真常元）
以为多个同种联结词串起来时结合顺序会改变真值，因而不承认可以不写括号

nodes.title: 可满足性与不可满足性（satisfiability）
misconceptions: 找到一组使其为真的赋值后，就宣称它是永真式（可满足不等于永真）
为证明不可满足只验证了几组赋值都为假，没有覆盖全部赋值
把「原式不可满足」与「原式的否定不可满足」混淆（原式不可满足等价于其否定是永真式）
认为永真式不算可满足

nodes.title: 对偶式（dual）
misconceptions: 把对偶式当成否定式：求对偶只交换合取与析取、交换两个常元，不加否定号
对含条件联结词或双条件联结词的式子也照搬交换合取与析取（定义只覆盖只含析取、合取、否定的命题）
以为求两次对偶得到的是否定式，而不是原式

nodes.title: 功能完备的联结词集合（functionally complete）
misconceptions: 以为功能完备要求两个复合命题写法完全相同，而不是逻辑等价即可
以为只有「否定、合取、析取」这一组是完备的，忽略只用否定加合取、只用否定加析取、只用 NOR、只用 NAND 也完备
把 NAND 与 NOR 记反（NAND 只在两个成分都为真时为假，NOR 只在两个成分都为假时为真）
以为 NAND 可以结合，把两种不同加括号方式得到的式子当成等价

nodes.title: 用真值表判定两个复合命题是否逻辑等价
misconceptions: 只比较了部分行就下结论，没有覆盖全部取值组合
把两个待比较的式子算在同一列里，导致无法逐列对照
变元个数为 n 时行数算少（应为 2 的 n 次方行）
把两式真值列恰好相同的若干行当成「处处一致」

subgoals.label: 把「两式是否逻辑等价」改判为「对应的双条件式是否永真」
subgoals.source_line: The compound propositions p and q are called logically equivalent if p ↔q is a tautology.

subgoals.label: 并排算出两式的真值列，逐行比较两列是否处处一致
subgoals.source_line: One way to determine whether two compound propositions are equivalent is to use a truth table. In particular, the compound propositions p and q are equivalent if and only if the columns giving their truth values agree.

subgoals.label: 按固定顺序枚举所有真值组合，避免漏行或重复行
subgoals.source_line: These eight combinations of truth values are TTT, TTF, TFT, TFF, FTT, FTF, FFT, and FFF; we use this order when we display the rows of the truth table.

subgoals.label: 按变元个数确定表的规模（每多一个变元，取值组合数翻倍）

nodes.title: 用德摩根律求复合命题（含自然语言陈述）的否定
misconceptions: 取否定后没有把联结词换成相反的，直接把否定号「分配」进去
自然语言陈述没有先符号化就凭语感改写，导致析取/合取判断错
否定的结果仍然带着原来的联结词，或只否定了其中一个成分
把适用于两个成分的律直接推广时漏掉某些项的否定

subgoals.source_line: In particular, the equivalence ¬(p ∨q) ≡¬p ∧¬q tells us that the negation of a disjunction is formed by taking the conjunction of the negations of the component propositions.

subgoals.source_line: Similarly, the equivalence ¬(p ∧q) ≡¬p ∨¬q tells us that the negation of a conjunction is formed by taking the disjunction of the negations of the component propositions.

subgoals.source_line: When using De Morgan’s laws, remember to change the logical connective after you negate.

subgoals.source_line: Let r be “Heather will go to the concert” and s be “Steve will go to the concert.” Then “Heather will go to the concert or Steve will go to the concert” can be represented by r ∨s. By the second of De Morgan’s laws, ¬(r ∨s) is equivalent to ¬r ∧¬s.

subgoals.source_line: Furthermore, note that De Morgan’s laws extend to ¬(p1 ∨p2 ∨⋯∨pn) ≡(¬p1 ∧¬p2 ∧⋯∧¬pn)

nodes.title: 用已知等价律把待证式逐步化归，构造新的逻辑等价
misconceptions: 一步里同时用好几条等价式改写多处，出错后无法定位
把待证结论当作已知条件使用（用结论去替换式子）
改写时只变换了一边而另一边保持原样，最后两侧不同却宣布等价

subgoals.source_line: The reason for this is that a proposition in a compound proposition can be replaced by a compound proposition that is logically equivalent to it without changing the truth value of the original compound proposition.

nodes.title: 判定一个复合命题是否可满足（不依赖真值表的推理与工具方法）
misconceptions: 用几组赋值试不出真就宣布不可满足
把「否定式恒真」当作「原式恒真」
只对合取式中的一部分子句做了推理，漏掉其余子句的约束
变元稍多仍坚持手算真值表，忽略指数级增长

subgoals.label: 按定义区分「存在一组赋值使其为真」与「对所有赋值都为假」

subgoals.source_line: Note that a compound proposition is unsatisﬁable if and only if its negation is true for all assignments of truth values to the variables, that is, if and only if its negation is a tautology.

subgoals.label: 证明不可满足必须覆盖所有赋值，不能只举几组为假的例子
subgoals.source_line: However, to show that a compound proposition is unsatisﬁable, we need to show that every assignment of truth values to its variables makes it false.

subgoals.source_line: Finally, note that for (p ∨¬q) ∧(q ∨¬r) ∧(r ∨¬p) ∧(p ∨q ∨r) ∧(¬p ∨¬q ∨¬r) to be true, (p ∨¬q) ∧(q ∨¬r) ∧(r ∨¬p) and (p ∨q ∨r) ∧(¬p ∨¬q ∨¬r) must both be true.

subgoals.label: 变元很多时放弃真值表，改用计算机求解程序

nodes.title: 把约束型实际问题编码成可满足性问题并求解
misconceptions: 变元含义设计含糊，导致同一个变元被用来表示两件事
只写了「至少一个」类断言，漏掉「至多一个」类断言，得到的解不满足题目约束
把「至多一个」写成「所有候选都为假」，把该出现的那个也排除了

nodes.title: 命题函数与谓词（propositional function / predicate）
misconceptions: 把带自由变量的命题函数当成命题，说它有确定的真值

以为 ∃!xP(x) 也保证 ∀xP(x) 成立

以为展开时少列一个元素不影响真值

nodes.title: 约束变量、自由变量与量词辖域

把 ∀ 分配到析取、把 ∃ 分配到合取，当成普遍成立的等价式

∃y(B(x, y) ∧∀z((z ≠y) →¬B(x, z))).

nodes.title: 否定嵌套量词命题（把否定推进到谓词前）
misconceptions: 只把最外层量词取反就停下，没有把否定一路推到谓词前
把否定整句的嵌套量化写成量词不变、只给谓词加否定
否定落到蕴含上时对前件和后件分别取反，而不是用蕴含的否定等价式

nodes.title: 有效论证与论证形式（valid argument / argument form）
misconceptions: 把“前提全真则结论必真”的形式有效性，说成“结论事实上为真”——前提为假时论证照样有效，但结论不能保证为真
只检验某一次代入后结论的真假，而不检验“所有代入下前提真是否都逼出结论真”
把论证形式有效误认为是在断言前提本身为真

nodes.title: 推理规则（rules of inference）
misconceptions: 把“规则”当成待证明的结论而不是可反复套用的模板，每遇到一个论证都从真值表重新算一遍
把与真值表判定并列的推理规则当成“更弱的近似方法”，以为规则推出的结论只是可能真

nodes.title: 用真值表判定论证形式有效（truth table method）
misconceptions: 以为只要找出“使结论为真”的一行就证明了有效
变量稍多就硬列真值表，忽略 2^n 行的代价与用推理规则替代的必要性

subgoals.label: 按重言式判据写出待检验的蕴含式
subgoals.source_line: Remark: From the deﬁnition of a valid argument form we see that the argument form with premises p1, p2, … , pn and conclusion q is valid exactly when (p1 ∧p2 ∧⋯∧pn) →q is a tautology.

subgoals.label: 穷举赋值，找前提全真而结论为假的行
subgoals.source_line: We can always use a truth table to show that an argument form is valid. We do this by showing that whenever the premises are true, the conclusion must also be true. However, this can be a tedious approach.

subgoals.label: 从已证重言式读出规则，替代逐行穷举
subgoals.source_line: The tautology (p ∧(p →q)) →q is the basis of the rule of inference called modus ponens, or the law of detachment.

nodes.title: 假言推理 / 肯定前件（modus ponens）
misconceptions: 把肯定后件当成肯定前件使用：已知 p →q 与 q 就断言 p
条件句方向被读反，由 p →q 与 p 去推出前件不成立

nodes.title: 析取三段论（disjunctive syllogism）
misconceptions: 在二选一里误用否定去消去“结论的那一支”而不是被否定的那一支
忽略析取是相容的，未排除两支同真的情形就下断言

nodes.title: 判定一个论证用了哪条推理规则
misconceptions: 直接凭生活语义给论证贴规则标签，而不先把命题符号化再逐符号比对形式
把内容相近但形式不同的论证（如含传递的两步条件句）当成同一条规则

subgoals.label: 把论证的每个命题符号化
subgoals.source_line: In each argument, we ﬁrst use propositional variables to express the propositions in the argument.

subgoals.label: 写出论证形式
subgoals.source_line: We then show that the resulting argument form is a rule of inference from Table 1.

subgoals.label: 与已列出的规则模板逐一比对，指出所用规则
subgoals.source_line: State which rule of inference is the basis of the following argument: “It is below freezing now. Therefore, it is below freezing or raining now.”

nodes.title: 由前提构造有效论证（build an argument）
misconceptions: 只写结论不给每步理由，或理由写成“显然”
把结论的前提直接当成已获得的前提，中途引入没给出的假设
前提很多时仍拒绝分步，试图一步跳到结论

subgoals.label: 把英文论证符号化并写出前提与结论
subgoals.source_line: Then the premises are p →q, ¬p →r, and r →s. The desired conclusion is ¬q →s. We need to give a valid argument with premises p →q, ¬p →r, and r →s and conclusion ¬q →s.

subgoals.label: 逐步列出每行并标注依据
subgoals.source_line: This is illustrated by Examples 6 and 7, where the steps of arguments are displayed on separate lines, with the reason for each step explicitly stated.

subgoals.label: 把每一步归约到已确立的规则
subgoals.source_line: These examples also show how arguments in English can be analyzed using rules of inference.

subgoals.label: 把已证等价式（如逆否）当作中间步骤来用
subgoals.source_line: This argument form shows that the premises lead to the desired conclusion.
subgoals.not_in_source: 教材给出了 Example 7 的完整步骤表（其中把 (1) 换成其逆否命题再作假言三段论），但没有单列“何时该用逆否式替换条件句”的选步规则，需要在例题里自行归纳。

nodes.title: 谬误：肯定结论与否定假设（fallacies）
misconceptions: 由 p →q 与 q 推出 p（肯定结论）
由 p →q 与 ¬p 推出 ¬q（否定假设）
把“前提假”当成论证无效的理由，或反过来把“结论假”当成形式无效的证据

nodes.title: 识别并命名无效论证形式
misconceptions: 举出一个“结论碰巧为假”的实例当作形式无效的证明，而不是给出让前提全真结论为假的赋值
看出论证不对却说不出所用形式的名称与错因

subgoals.label: 给出前提全真而结论为假的一组赋值，说明它不是重言式
subgoals.source_line: The proposition ((p →q) ∧q) →p is not a tautology, because it is false when p is false and q is true.

subgoals.label: 把该形式归入已知谬误并指出错在哪一步
subgoals.source_line: This type of incorrect reasoning is called the fallacy of aﬃrming the conclusion.

nodes.title: 归结证明（resolution）
misconceptions: 把归结当成能直接作用于任意原句的规则，忘记必须先化子句
把 x ∨(y ∧z) 这样的合取误当成一个子句，不拆成两条
只用一条前提去归结，忽略两条前提各出一个互补文字才产生归结式

subgoals.label: 先把所有前提与结论化为子句
subgoals.source_line: To construct proofs in propositional logic using resolution as the only rule of inference, the hypotheses and the conclusion must be expressed as clauses, where a clause is a disjunction of variables or negations of these variables.

subgoals.label: 把非子句语句改写成等价子句
subgoals.source_line: We can replace a statement in propositional logic that is not a clause by one or more equivalent statements that are clauses.

subgoals.label: 消去互补文字，取其余文字的析取得归结式
subgoals.source_line: The ﬁnal disjunction in the resolution rule, q ∨r, is called the resolvent.

subgoals.label: 取两条子句归结，直到得到目标子句
subgoals.source_line: Using the two clauses p ∨r and ¬r ∨s, we can use resolution to conclude p ∨s.

nodes.title: 全称例示（universal instantiation）
misconceptions: 例示出的个体自带了原语句没说的性质（例如由“所有女性都睿智”推出 Lisa 还额外满足别的条件）
把全称例示与存在例示混用，以为 ∀xP(x) 可以给出一个“满足某个额外条件的 c”

nodes.title: 存在例示（existential instantiation）
misconceptions: 把存在例示出的见证元当成任意元素，对 c 附加额外假设
同一个见证元符号被两次存在例示复用，或把由存在例示得到的 c 再拿去作全称推广

nodes.title: 全称推广（universal generalization）
misconceptions: 所用的 c 是特殊的（某个具体个体或额外假设下的个体），却据此断言 ∀xP(x)
对元素 c 偷偷加上论证中未获授权的前提后再作全称推广

nodes.title: 存在推广（existential generalization）
misconceptions: 把只对某个特定个体成立的性质直接推广成对全体的断言
误以为存在推广要求掌握满足条件的具体是哪一个元素

nodes.title: 量词规则与命题规则的组合（universal modus ponens / universal modus tollens）
misconceptions: 把 a 当成被全称量词覆盖的任意元素，而不是域中一个确定的个体
拿一个不满足前件 P(a) 的 a 去使用该组合规则
看到 ∀x(P(x) →Q(x)) 与 ¬Q(a) 时误用肯定式去推 Q(a)

subgoals.label: 先做全称例示，得到该个体的条件句
subgoals.source_line: To see this, note that by universal instantiation, P(a) →Q(a) is true.

subgoals.label: 确认该个体满足全称条件句的前件
subgoals.source_line: This rule tells us that if ∀x(P(x) →Q(x)) is true, and if P(a) is true for a particular element a in the domain of the universal quantiﬁer, then Q(a) must also be true.

subgoals.label: 用肯定式得到该个体的结论
subgoals.source_line: It follows by universal modus ponens that Q(100) is true, namely, that 1002 < 2100.

nodes.title: 定理（theorem）
misconceptions: 把 1.1 里的命题（proposition，有真值的陈述句）与本节的命题（proposition，指不太重要的定理）当成同一回事
以为定理必须写成条件语句（教材指出定理也可以是完全不同形式的逻辑陈述）
把猜想当定理引用（猜想只是被提出为真的陈述，只有找到证明之后才成为定理）

nodes.title: 证明（proof）
misconceptions: 把公理也当成需要证明的命题（公理是被假定为真、无须证明的陈述）
随手引用没有证明过的结论或凭直觉跳步（构造证明时只能用公理、定义和已证结果这些事实）
以为每一步都必须显式写出所用规则（面向人类读者的证明几乎都是非形式证明：一步里可以用多条规则、可以跳步、不显式声明公理与推理规则）
以为证明不写全就会被判错（教材明确说若把每一步都写出来，证明会长得无法阅读）

nodes.title: 引理、推论与猜想（lemma, corollary, conjecture）
misconceptions: 以为引理本身就是不值钱的小结论（引理是为证明其他结果服务的辅助定理，复杂证明常先拆成一系列引理逐个证明）
把推论当成需要从头独立证明的新定理（推论是可以直接从已证定理得到的）
把猜想当成定理来引用（猜想在被证明之前不是定理，而且很多猜想最后被证明是假的）

nodes.title: 偶数、奇数与奇偶性（even, odd, parity）
misconceptions: 以为一个整数可以既是偶数又是奇数（定义明确说每个整数非偶即奇，且不会既偶又奇）
只把“是奇数”当成一个性质而不展开成可代入运算的形式（必须写成比某个整数大一倍的样子才能继续计算）
在逆否证明里把“不是奇数”当成不好用的否定式（在整数范围内它就是偶数，可以直接展开继续推导）

nodes.title: 有理数与无理数（rational, irrational）
misconceptions: 忽略分母不能为零这一条（定义要求存在整数之比且分母非零）
把“不是有理数”当成一种正面描述，而不是“不存在满足条件的整数之比”这一否定（证明无理数要从假设能写成整数之比出发导出矛盾）
证明根号 2 无理时忘记把那个分数先约到最低项，于是最后得不到“分子分母同为偶数”与“互素”的对撞

nodes.title: 证明中的常见错误（mistakes in proofs）
misconceptions: 由“若前件成立则后件成立”加上后件成立，反推前件成立（肯定结论的谬误）
由“若前件成立则后件成立”加上前件不成立，推出后件不成立（否定假设的谬误；正确的方向是逆否命题）
把要证的结论直接当前提用（循环论证：在证明过程中直接假设结论的等价说法成立，却不给任何理由）
在等式两边除以一个可能为零的式子（经典假证明里正是除以了一个等于零的差）
把算术与代数上的粗心错误当成逻辑错误，或反过来只查逻辑不查每一处计算

nodes.title: 证明全称量化的条件语句

subgoals.label: 看清定理省略了全称量词，按“对论域中所有元素都成立”来读
subgoals.source_line: Many theorems assert that a property holds for all elements in a domain, such as the integers or the real numbers. Although the precise statement of such theo-rems needs to include a universal quantiﬁer, the standard convention in mathematics is to omit it.

subgoals.label: 取论域中一个任意元素，把目标降为该元素上的条件语句
subgoals.source_line: To prove a theorem of the form ∀x(P(x) →Q(x)), our goal is to show that P(c) →Q(c) is true, where c is an arbitrary element of the domain, and then apply universal generalization.

subgoals.label: 证完任意元素后引用全称推广，把结论提升到整个论域
subgoals.source_line: Finally, universal generalization implies that the theorem holds for all members of the domain.

nodes.title: 直接证明（direct proof）

subgoals.label: 假设前件为真，再用公理、定义、已证定理和推理规则推向结论
subgoals.source_line: In a direct proof, we assume that p is true and use axioms, deﬁnitions, and previously proven theorems, together with rules of inference, to show that q must also be true.

subgoals.label: 后续各步由推理规则接续，最后一步落到后件为真
subgoals.source_line: subsequent steps are constructed using rules of inference, with the ﬁnal step showing that q must also be true.

subgoals.label: 收尾时最后一步直接写出定理的结论
subgoals.source_line: In practice, the ﬁnal step of a proof is usually just the conclusion of the theorem.

nodes.title: 逆否证明（proof by contraposition）

subgoals.label: 确认可以改用逆否命题：原条件语句与逆否命题等价
subgoals.source_line: Proofs by contraposition make use of the fact that the conditional statement p →q is equivalent to its contrapositive, ¬q →¬p.

subgoals.label: 把结论的否定取为前提，用公理、定义、已证定理推出前提的否定
subgoals.source_line: In a proof by contraposition of p →q, we take ¬q as a premise, and using axioms, deﬁnitions, and previously proven theorems, together with rules of inference, we show that ¬p must follow.

subgoals.label: 先把“结论为假”翻译成正面说法，变成可以展开计算的形式
subgoals.source_line: The ﬁrst step in a proof by contraposition is to assume that the conclusion of the conditional statement “If 3n + 2 is odd, then n is odd” is false; namely, assume that n is even.

subgoals.label: 推出前提为假后，据此断定原条件语句为真
subgoals.source_line: Because the negation of the conclusion of the conditional statement implies that the hypothesis is false, the original conditional statement is true.

nodes.title: 空证明（vacuous proof）

subgoals.label: 先确认假设本身是假的（假设为假时条件语句必真）
subgoals.source_line: We can quickly prove that a conditional statement p →q is true when we know that p is false, because p →q must be true when p is false.

subgoals.label: 证出假设为假即完成整条证明
subgoals.source_line: Con-sequently, if we can show that p is false, then we have a proof, called a vacuous proof, of the conditional statement p →q.

subgoals.label: 不去讨论结论的真假，它不影响条件语句的真值
subgoals.source_line: The fact that the conclusion of this conditional statement, 02 > 0, is false is irrelevant to the truth value of the conditional statement, because a conditional statement with a false hypothesis is guaranteed to be true.

nodes.title: 平凡证明（trivial proof）

subgoals.label: 先确认结论已经为真
subgoals.source_line: We can also quickly prove a conditional statement p →q if we know that the conclusion q is true.

subgoals.label: 证明结论为真即完成整条证明
subgoals.source_line: By showing that q is true, it follows that p →q must also be true. A proof of p →q that uses the fact that q is true is called a trivial proof.

subgoals.label: 整个证明中不需要用到假设
subgoals.source_line: Note that the hypothesis, which is the statement “a ≥b,” was not needed in this proof.

nodes.title: 反证法（proof by contradiction）

subgoals.label: 把待证命题的否定设为假设，目标是导出某个自相矛盾的结论
subgoals.source_line: Because the statement r ∧¬r is a contradiction whenever r is a proposition, we can prove that p is true if we can show that ¬p →(r ∧¬r) is true for some proposition r.

subgoals.label: 待证的是条件语句时，改为假设“前提与结论的否定”同时为真，由它们推出矛盾
subgoals.source_line: Proof by contradiction can be used to prove conditional statements. In such proofs, we ﬁrst assume the negation of the conclusion. We then use the premises of the theorem and the negation of the conclusion to arrive at a contradiction.

subgoals.label: 手上已有一条逆否证明时，补上原前提作为额外假设即可改写成反证
subgoals.source_line: To rewrite a proof by contraposition of p →q as a proof by contradiction, we suppose that both p and ¬q are true.

subgoals.label: 导出矛盾后据此断定原命题成立
subgoals.source_line: Because q is false, but ¬p →q is true, we can conclude that ¬p is false, which means that p is true.

nodes.title: 证明等价（双条件与多命题等价）

subgoals.label: 把双条件拆成两个方向，分别证明两个条件语句
subgoals.source_line: To prove a theorem that is a biconditional statement, that is, a statement of the form p ↔q, we show that p →q and q →p are both true.

subgoals.label: 命题多于两个时，只需证出一圈首尾相接的蕴含链
subgoals.source_line: This shows that if the n conditional statements p1 →p2, p2 →p3, … , pn →p1 can be shown to be true, then the propositions p1, p2, … , pn are all equivalent.

subgoals.label: 链条的顺序和起点可以自选，只要沿链能从任一命题走到任何另一命题
subgoals.source_line: When we prove that a group of statements are equivalent, we can establish any chain of conditional statements we choose as long as it is possible to work through the chain to go from any one of these statements to any other statement.

nodes.title: 选择证明方法的策略

subgoals.label: 拿到全称条件语句先评估直接证明是否可行
subgoals.source_line: When you want to prove a statement of the form ∀x(P(x) →Q(x)), ﬁrst evaluate whether a direct proof looks promising.

subgoals.label: 先展开假设里的定义，再用公理与手头定理往下推
subgoals.source_line: Begin by expanding the deﬁnitions in the hypotheses. Start to reason using these hypotheses, together with axioms and available theorems.

subgoals.label: 直接证明走不通时，换成逆否证明再试一遍
subgoals.source_line: If a direct proof does not seem to go anywhere, for instance when there is no clear way to use hypotheses as in Examples 3 and 4 to reach the conclusion, try the same thing with a proof by contraposition.

subgoals.label: 假设本身难以利用时（否定式、非零之类的条件），提示该走间接证明
subgoals.source_line: (Hypotheses such as x is irrational or x ≠0 that are diﬃcult to reason from are a clue that an indirect proof might be your best best.)

nodes.title: 用反例反驳全称命题

subgoals.label: 要驳倒全称命题，只需给出一个使它为假的具体例子
subgoals.source_line: to show that a statement of the form ∀xP(x) is false, we need only ﬁnd a counterexample, that is, an example x for which P(x) is false.

subgoals.label: 命题看似为假或反复证不出来时，转为去找反例
subgoals.source_line: When presented with a statement of the form ∀xP(x), which we believe to be false or which has resisted all proof attempts, we look for a counterexample.

subgoals.label: 验证候选反例：穷举相关取值，说明它确实不满足该性质
subgoals.source_line: note that the only perfect squares not exceeding 3 are 02 = 0 and 12 = 1. Furthermore, there is no way to get 3 as the sum of two terms each of which is 0 or 1.

nodes.title: 分情形证明（proof by cases）
misconceptions: 漏掉某个情形就宣布证完：讨论正负时漏掉等于零的那种情况（Example 9 的假证明就败在这里）
只验证了若干例子就当成覆盖了所有情形，把没证全的命题当定理用

subgoals.label: 把前提改写成覆盖全部可能的若干情形，再逐个情形证明同一个结论
subgoals.source_line: [(p1 ∨p2 ∨⋯∨pn) →q] ↔[(p1 →q) ∧(p2 →q) ∧⋯∧(pn →q)] can be used as a rule of inference. This shows that the original conditional statement with a hypothesis made up of a disjunction of the propositions p1, p2, … , pn can be proved by proving each of the n conditional statements pi →q, i = 1, 2, … , n, individually.

subgoals.label: 确认所分情形合起来覆盖所有可能（漏掉一个情形，证明就作废）
subgoals.source_line: A proof by cases must cover all possible cases that arise in a theorem.

subgoals.label: 判断值不值得分情形：没有明显入手点、而分情形能带来额外信息时才用
subgoals.source_line: Generally, look for a proof by cases when there is no obvious way to begin a proof, but when extra information in each case helps move the proof forward.

nodes.title: 穷举证明（exhaustive proof / proof by exhaustion）
misconceptions: 把所有想得到的例子都验证过就当成证明了（正整数写成 18 个四次方之和，79 就是反例）

subgoals.label: 先确认要检查的实例数目足够少、真的能一个个列完
subgoals.source_line: People can carry out exhaustive proofs when it is necessary to check only a relatively small number of instances of a statement.

subgoals.label: 把每个允许的取值当成一个情形，逐个验证结论都成立
subgoals.source_line: An exhaustive proof is a special type of proof by cases where each case involves checking a single example.

subgoals.label: 先缩小候选范围、排除不可能的取值，再对剩下的少数情形逐一检查
subgoals.source_line: We can quickly reduce a proof to checking just a few simple cases because x2 > 8 when |x| ≥3 and 3y2 > 8 when |y| ≥2. This leaves the cases when x equals −2, −1, 0, 1, or 2 and y equals −1, 0, or 1.

subgoals.label: 判断能不能穷举：无法列出全部实例时，再多计算机验证也算不上证明
subgoals.source_line: Note that not even a computer can check all instances when it is impossible to list all instances to check.

nodes.title: 不失一般性（without loss of generality, WLOG）
misconceptions: 对并不对称的情形也写「不失一般性」，把没证的情形当成「同理」，结果证明不完整
把「不失一般性」理解成「只要证随便挑的一个特例」，说不出其余情形为什么能照样推出

subgoals.label: 只详细证一个情形，并说明其余情形做同样的改动就能得到
subgoals.source_line: Implicit in this statement is that we can complete the case with x < 0 and y ≥0 using the same argument as we used for the case with x ≥0 and y < 0, but with the obvious changes.

subgoals.label: 写「不失一般性」时要能指出各情形之间靠什么互换互推，把理由交代清楚
subgoals.source_line: (Note that our use of without loss of generality within the proof is justiﬁed because the proof when y is odd can be obtained by simply interchanging the roles of x and y in the proof we have given.)

subgoals.label: 检查情形之间是否真对称：某个情形差别很大时就不能略过它
subgoals.source_line: Sometimes assumptions are made that lead to a loss in generality. Such assumptions can be made that do not take into account that one case may be substantially diﬀerent from others. This can lead to an incomplete, and possibly unsalvageable, proof.

nodes.title: 存在性证明（existence proof）
misconceptions: 认为没把那个元素具体算出来的证明不算证明（其实非构造性的存在性证明同样成立）

nodes.title: 构造性存在性证明（constructive existence proof）
misconceptions: 只算出或猜到某个候选对象，却不验证它满足所要求的性质，就宣布证明结束

subgoals.label: 找出一个具体的元素（见证元），并验证它满足所要求的性质
subgoals.source_line: Sometimes an existence proof of ∃xP(x) can be given by ﬁnding an element a, called a witness, such that P(a) is true. This type of existence proof is called constructive.

subgoals.label: 把找到的对象摆出来并说明它符合要求，存在性就算证完
subgoals.source_line: The existence of one such tiling completes a constructive existence proof.

nodes.title: 非构造性存在性证明（nonconstructive existence proof）
misconceptions: 在非构造性证明里以为自己已经找到了那个元素（其实只证了必有一个）

subgoals.label: 不去找具体元素，改用别的方式证明存在性
subgoals.source_line: It is also possible to give an existence proof that is nonconstructive; that is, we do not ﬁnd an element a such that P(a) is true, but rather prove that ∃xP(x) is true in some other way.

subgoals.label: 常用手段是用反证法：否定存在量化，推出矛盾
subgoals.source_line: One common method of giving a nonconstructive existence proof is to use proof by contradiction and show that the negation of the existential quantiﬁcation implies a contradiction.

subgoals.label: 确认「只证存在、不指出是哪一个」也算完成证明
subgoals.source_line: Note that we showed that a winning strategy exists, but we did not specify an actual winning strategy. Consequently, the proof is a nonconstructive existence proof.

nodes.title: 唯一性证明（uniqueness proof）
misconceptions: 只证了唯一性（任意两个满足条件的对象相等）就宣布「存在唯一」，漏掉存在性这一半
把「我找到了一个解」当成唯一性证明，没说明不会有第二个

subgoals.label: 存在性部分：先证明确实有一个元素满足所要求的性质
subgoals.source_line: Existence: We show that an element x with the desired property exists.

subgoals.label: 唯一性部分：假设两个元素都满足性质，推出它们相等
subgoals.source_line: Uniqueness: We show that if x and y both have the desired property, then x = y.

subgoals.label: 必要时把目标写成量词形式：存在一个满足性质、其余都不满足
subgoals.source_line: Remark: Showing that there is a unique element x such that P(x) is the same as proving the statement ∃x(P(x) ∧∀y(y ≠x →¬P(y))).

nodes.title: 前向推理（forward reasoning）
misconceptions: 结论很复杂时硬着头皮从头往前推，写了很多步也到不了结论（这时应换逆向推理）

subgoals.label: 从前提出发，配合公理和已知定理一步步推向结论
subgoals.source_line: To begin a direct proof of a conditional statement, you start with the premises. Using these premises, together with axioms and known theorems, you can construct a proof using a sequence of steps that leads to the conclusion. This type of reasoning, called forward reasoning, is the most common type of reasoning used to prove relatively simple results.

subgoals.label: 间接证明时换起点：从结论的否定出发，一步步推出前提的否定
subgoals.source_line: Similarly, with indirect reasoning you can start with the negation of the conclusion and, using a sequence of steps, obtain the negation of the premises.

subgoals.label: 判断前向推理够不够用：结论复杂、路径看不出来时就要换方法
subgoals.source_line: Unfortunately, forward reasoning is often diﬃcult to use to prove more complicated results, because the reasoning needed to reach the desired conclusion may be far from obvious.

nodes.title: 逆向推理（backward reasoning）
misconceptions: 从结论出发时把方向用反：拿「结论能推出的东西」成立来说明结论成立（循环论证/乞题）
把逆向推理的草稿直接当正式证明交上去，没有倒过来写成前向证明

subgoals.label: 从要证的结论往回找：找一个已经能证明、且能推出结论的命题
subgoals.source_line: In such cases it may be helpful to use backward reasoning. To reason backward to prove a statement q, we ﬁnd a statement p that we can prove with the property that p →q.

subgoals.label: 别把推出方向搞反：不能由结论推出来的东西成立反过来断定结论成立
subgoals.source_line: (Note that it is not helpful to ﬁnd a statement r that you can prove such that q →r, because it is the fallacy of begging the question to conclude from q →r and r that q is true.)

subgoals.label: 把结论改写成一串彼此等价的式子，一直化到已知为真的式子
subgoals.source_line: To prove that (x + y)∕2 > √xy when x and y are distinct positive real numbers, we can work backward. We construct a sequence of equivalent inequalities.

subgoals.label: 逆推只是找路：最后把步骤倒过来，用前向推理写出正式证明
subgoals.source_line: Once we have carried out this backward reasoning, we can build a proof based on reversing the steps.

nodes.title: 改造已有证明（adapting existing proofs）
misconceptions: 碰到新定理完全从零开始，不去找结构相近的老定理和它的证明

subgoals.label: 先找结构相似的老结论，看它的证明能不能直接搬过来用
subgoals.source_line: An excellent way to look for possible approaches that can be used to prove a statement is to take advantage of existing proofs of similar results.

subgoals.label: 整段搬不动时，至少借用老证明里的想法
subgoals.source_line: Often an existing proof can be adapted to prove other facts. Even when this is not the case, some of the ideas used in existing proofs may be helpful.

subgoals.label: 照搬之后标出哪些步骤在新定理里还缺依据、需要另补工具
subgoals.source_line: In turns out that we can, but we need some ammunition from number theory, which we will develop in Chapter 4. We sketch out the remainder of the proof, but leave the justiﬁcation of these steps until Chapter 4.

nodes.title: 寻找反例（looking for counterexamples）
misconceptions: 试了很多个小例子都成立就断言命题为真（正整数写成 18 个四次方之和，79 处就失败）

subgoals.label: 先尝试证明；证不出来就从最小的例子开始找反例；还找不到就回头继续证
subgoals.source_line: When confronted with a conjecture, you might ﬁrst try to prove this conjecture, and if your attempts are unsuccessful, you might try to ﬁnd a counterexample, ﬁrst by looking at the simplest, smallest examples. If you cannot ﬁnd a counterexample, you might again try to prove the statement.

subgoals.label: 找反例的具体打法：把正整数按从小到大逐个代进去试
subgoals.source_line: To look for a counterexample, we try to write successive positive integers as a sum of three squares.

subgoals.label: 找到可疑的对象后，把可能的取值限制住，证明它确实不满足命题
subgoals.source_line: To show that there are not three squares that add up to 7, we note that the only possible squares we can use are those not exceeding 7, namely, 0, 1, and 4. Because no three terms where each term is 0, 1, or 4 add up to 7, it follows that 7 is a counterexample.

nodes.title: 棋盘与铺砌（checkerboard / board / domino / tiling）
misconceptions: 只比较棋子数或格子数的奇偶就下结论：格子数是偶数只是必要条件，62 格的棋盘照样可能铺不出来

nodes.title: 染色计数论证（coloring argument）
misconceptions: 只数格子总数，忘了按颜色分别计数，于是看不出「每种颜色各需多少格」这个矛盾

subgoals.label: 把棋盘交替染色，并观察每块骨牌覆盖各种颜色各几个
subgoals.source_line: We color the squares of this checkerboard using alternating white and black squares, as in Figure 2. Observe that a domino in a tiling of such a board covers one white square and one black square.

subgoals.label: 由「每块骨牌覆盖一黑一白」算出整块棋盘要铺满必须有多少黑格、多少白格
subgoals.source_line: Note that each domino in this tiling covers one white and one black square. Consequently, the tiling covers 31 white squares and 31 black squares.

subgoals.label: 假设铺砌存在，推出它与染色计数矛盾，从而否定存在性
subgoals.source_line: We can use these observations to prove by contradiction that a standard checkerboard with opposite corners removed cannot be tiled using dominoes.

subgoals.label: 换骨牌类型就换颜色数：用三格骨牌时改成三色染色
subgoals.source_line: Because we are using straight triominoes rather than dominoes, we color the squares using three colors rather than two colors

subgoals.label: 观察每块三格骨牌覆盖三种颜色各一个
subgoals.source_line: Next, we make the crucial observation that when a straight triomino covers three squares of the checkerboard, it covers one blue square, one black square, and one white square.

subgoals.label: 用旋转对称把缺格统一成同一种颜色，减少要讨论的情形
subgoals.source_line: Thus, without loss of generality, we may assume that we have rotated the coloring so that the missing square is colored blue.

nodes.title: 未解决问题与猜想（open problems）
misconceptions: 把「已经被计算机验证到很大范围」当成「已经证明」（3x + 1 猜想验到 5.48 ⋅1018 仍未证明）
